title: Build SEO Pro Custom: customisation loader, Site Health, CLI, client README, upstream request form and DCO
body:
## What

Turn the fresh starter copy into **SEO Pro Custom**: an empty plugin installed on every client site, and the public template each client copies into their own private repository for their site's own customisations.

Design approved by the owner on 10 November 2026; everything a worker needs is below. Start from `main` after the rename PR (#4: SEO Pro Custom, `seoprocustom`, prefixes `SEOProCustom` / `SEOPROCUSTOM` / CSS `spc`) is merged; the repository was renamed from `seoprostackcustom` on 10 November 2026. The repository is a GitHub template repository (clients use **Use this template**).

Related: supported-hook lists being written for SEO Pro Stack (wpallstars/seoprostack#1489) and the paid products; link to SEO Pro Stack's `docs/HOOKS.md` from the README once it exists.

## How

1. **Loader** (`includes/features/` class listed in the setup's `FEATURES`, per `STANDARDS.md`): loads `customizations/*.php` one file at a time, each with a header read by `get_file_data()`:
   - `Description:` what and why.
   - `Sites:` `all` (default), or comma-separated blog IDs or hosts (multisite).
   - `Requires:` e.g. `plugin-a >= 0.4.137, plugin-b >= 0.1.45` (plugin slug or theme stylesheet, `version_compare`). Not met: the file is skipped.
   - `Upstream:` the request's issue URL.
   - `Retire-When:` same syntax as `Requires:`. Met: the file is no longer loaded.
   - Optional `{name}.css` / `{name}.js` next to the file, enqueued after the theme's styles (the PSD child theme's `site-design.css` handle) on the front end, versioned by file time.
   - A file with a PHP syntax error must be reported and skipped, not stop the site: lint before include where `php -l` is unavailable on hosts (token_get_all with `TOKEN_PARSE` in a try/catch for `ParseError`), cache the result by file mtime.
2. **Site Health test** listing each customisation: loaded, skipped (requirement not met), retired ("upstream now does this; delete the file"), or failed (syntax error). Also on the plugin's settings screen as a card.
3. **WP-CLI** `wp seoprocustom list [--format=json]` with the same states, for the fleet check.
4. `customizations/example.php` showing a filter and a CSS file, disabled (e.g. `Requires: never`), plus `customizations/README.md`.
5. **`AGENTS.md`** rules for a client's AI: prefer an upstream setting, then a documented filter/action, then CSS, then code; never copy or edit upstream files; never write options or theme mods while loading (the theme's `settings compare`, `follow-defaults` and `restore` must see nothing); one-off data changes only as WP-CLI commands with `--dry-run` and a backup; no new tables; no secrets in Git; one file per customisation with the headers above.
6. **README for clients**: what it is; make your own private copy with **Use this template** (a fork of a public repository stays public); set `GitHub Plugin URI` / `Update URI` to your repository; read-only fine-grained token for that one repository in `WPALLSTARS_GITHUB_TOKEN` (wp-config.php, never Git); release and click Update; how to request upstream changes (below); `scripts/sync-core.sh` / starter-sync for our later loader changes.
7. **Upstream requests**: issue form `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/product-request.yml` for the private products (PSD child theme, SEO Pro Directory): product, the customisation file it would replace, what and why; a warning that issues are public (no site addresses, private code or client data; use Tools → Report a problem for anything sensitive). Public products (SEO Pro Stack, the starters) take issues and PRs on their own repositories; say so in `config.yml` contact links.
8. **DCO**: `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for `Signed-off-by:` on contributed commits (GPL-3.0 code we may ship in paid products); add a DCO check workflow for pull requests.
9. Make it the plugin's own per `~/.aidevops/agents/tools/wordpress/wp-plugin-new.md` step 6 if the identity PR has not: README (keep the badges block), `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`, `LAUNCH.md`, banner.

## Acceptance

- `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass; the smoke test loads a customisation, skips one with an unmet `Requires:`, retires one with a met `Retire-When:`, and reports (not fatals on) one with a syntax error.
- With no customisations the plugin adds no front-end output and no queries.
- `wp seoprocustom list --format=json` shows the four states.
- First release `0.1.0` per `RELEASING.md` once merged (owner approved the public template).

### Files Scope

- includes/features/
- includes/class-seoprocustom-setup.php
- customizations/
- scripts/smoke-test.sh
- .distignore
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/
- .github/workflows/
- AGENTS.md
- README.md
- readme.txt
- changelog.txt
- CHANGELOG.md
- CONTRIBUTING.md
- LAUNCH.md

title: Customisations card: padding, spacing and no starter placeholder on the General tab
body:
## What

On **Settings → SEO Pro Custom → General**, the Customisations card looks unfinished (seen in `.wordpress-org/screenshot-1.png` from PR #7):

1. The card has no inner padding: the `Customisations` heading sits on the card's left edge and the table runs edge to edge.
2. It touches the "No settings yet" card above it, with no gap.
3. The tab says "SEO Pro Custom's settings appear here as features are added." and shows "No settings yet." That is the starter's placeholder. SEO Pro Custom has no settings of its own, so the General tab should lead with the Customisations card and one line saying where the files go (`customizations/` in your own copy; link the Read Me tab).

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprocustom-customizations.php` → `render_card()` (around lines 485–522): the card markup (`spc-cards` / `spc-card`, `h3`, `table.widefat`).
- `includes/class-seoprocustom-setup.php`: the General tab's description and empty state, if they are set there (plugin-specific file, per `STANDARDS.md` → Structure).
- Style: `admin/css/seoprocustom-admin.css` is a starter core file (`scripts/sync-core.sh` keeps it the same as the starter's), so don't edit it. Use the existing card classes the setting cards use (for example the padded panel or `spc-empty` patterns), or a plugin-own stylesheet if the starter provides one for plugin-specific CSS. If neither works, propose the class upstream on the starter instead.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprocustom-customizations.php`
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprocustom-setup.php`
- EDIT: `.wordpress-org/screenshot-1.png`
- EDIT: `admin/images/screenshot-1.webp`

## Reference pattern

The setting cards on the same screen (`.spc-setting`) and `.spc-empty` (padding `16px 20px`) in `admin/css/seoprocustom-admin.css`.

## Verification

- `scripts/test-site.sh up --ref HEAD`, then put a few demo files in `wp-content/plugins/seoprocustom/customizations/` on the test site only (one loaded, one skipped by `Requires:`, one with `Retire-When:` met, one with a runtime error). `wp seoprocustom list` shows each state.
- The General tab shows the card padded like the other cards, with a gap from anything above it and no "No settings yet" placeholder.
- Check light and dark colour modes (the header's toggle).
- Retake `.wordpress-org/screenshot-1.png` at 1280×720 and run `scripts/build-banner.sh` to refresh `admin/images/screenshot-1.webp`.
- CI passes (lint, smoke test, release build, preflight and Plugin Check).

title: Keep the build's changes to starter core files through Starter sync; licence headers on the examples
body:
## What

`scripts/preflight-release.sh` (run on PR #9's branch) warns that four **starter core files** were changed in this plugin by the #2 build (PR #6). The daily Starter sync, or `scripts/sync-core.sh`, will put the starter's versions back and lose these changes:

- `scripts/smoke-test.sh`: the customisation loader checks (loaded, skipped, retired and failed demo files, around line 390–405).
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`: the issue chooser that points to the Product request form.
- `.gitignore`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: step 6, the DCO sign-off.

It also warns that `customizations/example.php` and `customizations/example.css` lack the SPDX, copyright, ATTRIBUTION.txt pointer and Provenance lines every shipped source file has.

## How

For each core file, choose one:

1. **Plugin-only lines go in `spc-own` blocks** (`<!-- spc-own:start -->` / `<!-- spc-own:end -->` in Markdown, the comment form the file type uses elsewhere; see how `RELEASING.md` has an empty `spc-own` block at step 2, and `STANDARDS.md` → Structure for the rule). `sync-core.sh` keeps those blocks, but only where the starter's file already has an empty own block at that place (`own_merge()` in `scripts/sync-core.sh` fails with "target has more own blocks than the starter"). Where the starter has none, first add an empty `spc-own`-style placeholder to the starter's file (a starter PR), then fill it here.
2. Or, where the change helps every plugin (likely `.gitignore`, perhaps a hook in `smoke-test.sh` for plugin-own checks), propose it on the starter (`wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding`) and leave this plugin's copy to match after the starter releases.

Then confirm `scripts/sync-core.sh --check` reports nothing for these four files.

For the examples: add the same header lines other source files have (`scripts/provenance.sh stamp` adds Provenance), keeping the example's own comment and headers readable for clients who copy it.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `scripts/smoke-test.sh`
- EDIT: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`
- EDIT: `.gitignore`
- EDIT: `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- EDIT: `customizations/example.php`
- EDIT: `customizations/example.css`

## Verification

- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: no "Core files" or "Licence" warnings for these files.
- `scripts/sync-core.sh --check`: these files match, or differ only inside `spc-own` blocks.
- CI's smoke test still runs the customisation checks (loaded, skipped, retired, failed).
- If anything goes to the starter, link the starter PR here.

## What

Run scripts/sync-core.sh, or change the starter first. Core files are the same in every plugin made from the starter, apart from the names (STANDARDS.md → Structure).

## How

1. Next to this repository: `git clone https://github.com/wpallstars/wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding.git` (or `git -C ../wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding pull`).
2. Here, on a branch: `scripts/sync-core.sh --from ../wp-plugin-starter-template-for-ai-coding`, then review `git diff`.
3. Each file's class says what a sync does with it (DEVELOPMENT.md → Starter sync): **behind** and **missing** files are updated or added. A file **changed here** holds a change this plugin made that no starter version has: it goes into the starter first (a pull request, or an issue there with this plugin's case); sync after it is merged there, with `--discard-local`. Never keep a plugin-only change in a core file: move it to this plugin's own files or its own blocks. A **newer** file has a starter version the starter's default branch does not contain: sync from a starter ref that does. While a file is changed here or newer, a sync writes nothing.
4. Read the starter's `changelog.txt` since this plugin last synced, for changes that need work in this plugin's own files (its Setup class, `phpstan-plugin.neon`, `.distignore` entries, README or readme.txt sections).
5. `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass; add a changelog line; open a pull request.

The daily Starter sync workflow (`.github/workflows/starter-sync.yml`) updates this issue while files differ and closes it once they match.
